business_patterns.top_pattern: CA acute hospital spend pressure in Medicaid products
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA Medicaid / ACUTE HOSPITAL / TANF Standard and LTSS Non Dual
key_driver_codes: Inguinal and Femoral Hernia Procedures without CC/MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA acute hospital spend increased across two Medicaid products, led by connective tissue and hernia admissions. Both claim counts and paid per admit rose, so this is not only a reimbursement issue. The repeat appearance of the same high-cost DRG across products suggests a targeted inpatient management and payment issue in CA acute hospitals.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is the largest operational pattern and is actionable through inpatient management and payment review in one state and facility setting.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Launch CA acute inpatient review on the identified TANF Standard and LTSS Non Dual claims, checking inpatient criteria, level of care, and payment terms for the flagged DRGs.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is still concentrated in a small number of low-baseline claims, so claim-level confirmation is needed before broad policy action.
evidence_summary: CA ACUTE HOSPITAL / TANF Standard added about $188K, led by Connective Tissue Disorders with MCC at about $178K on 2 claims.
CA ACUTE HOSPITAL / LTSS Non Dual added about $69K, again concentrated in Connective Tissue Disorders with MCC on 3 claims.
A smaller CA TANF Standard hernia episode added about $10K on 1 claim, reinforcing the acute inpatient pattern.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA single catastrophic IP Med/Surg outlier
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / IP Med/Surg / Connective Tissue Disorders with MCC

impact_summary.volume_signal: claims up from a very low base

business_patterns.pattern_details: CA also has a separate single-case IP Med/Surg spike. One Connective Tissue Disorders with MCC admission tied to diagnosis M3119 drove nearly the full increase. Because the change comes from one very high-cost case, this should be handled as a case-level outlier review rather than a broad policy response.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A single catastrophic admission can materially move cost and may present immediate recovery or case-management opportunity.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Perform claim-level clinical and payment audit on the M3119 admission to confirm diagnosis severity, inpatient payment logic, and any recoverable overpayment.
business_patterns.validation_reason: This pattern is driven by one claim, so action should wait for single-case validation.
evidence_summary: One CA IP Med/Surg case tied to M3119 and Connective Tissue Disorders with MCC drove about $156K.
The increase was concentrated in 1 claim with paid per admit up about $155.7K.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA nursing facility and SNF rare-case concentration
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / NF and SNF - FREE STANDING / LTSS Non Dual
key_driver_codes: Other Digestive System Diagnoses without CC/MCC

impact_summary.volume_signal: claims up from a low base

business_patterns.pattern_details: CA NF spend is being pushed by a cluster of rare diagnoses, and the same market also shows added SNF pressure in LTSS Non Dual. The NF signal is concentrated in feeding tube or ostomy, digestive, and connective tissue diagnoses, while SNF spend is concentrated in digestive and connective tissue DRGs. Together this points to a post-acute and nursing-facility management issue in CA rather than a broad statewide trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Post-acute concentration can drive avoidable spend through placement, length-of-stay, and payment-rule leakage if not addressed early.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a CA post-acute review that links NF episodes to SNF utilization for the flagged diagnoses, and verify whether placement, length of stay, and SNF payment rules were appropriate.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The signal comes from low-baseline rare cases, and the operational and clinical views may overlap, so claim-level linkage is needed before sizing broad intervention.
evidence_summary: CA NF rare cases totaled about $180K, led by M069 at about $69K on 3 claims and Z431 at about $37K on 10 claims.
Additional CA NF diagnoses M359, K9423, and K611 added about $75K combined.
CA LTSS Non Dual / SNF - FREE STANDING added about $54K, concentrated in Other Digestive System Diagnoses without CC/MCC and Connective Tissue Disorders with MCC.

business_patterns.top_pattern: FL and WA small-volume acute inpatient emergence
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: FL and WA / TANF Standard / ACUTE HOSPITAL and IP Med/Surg
key_driver_codes: Traumatic Stupor and Coma <1 Hour without CC/MCC

impact_summary.volume_signal: claims up from a low base

business_patterns.pattern_details: FL and WA show small numbers of acute inpatient cases creating visible spend movement. The pattern is concentrated in trauma and hernia-related IP Med/Surg admissions and appears again in TANF Standard acute hospital claims. This is an emergence pattern from a low base, so action should stay targeted to case review and inpatient criteria rather than broad benefit changes.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Small-volume inpatient outliers can expand quickly if they are not caught early, especially in acute hospital settings.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Send the FL and WA cases to UM operations for targeted inpatient medical-necessity and payment review on the identified trauma and hernia admissions.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is driven by a handful of claims across two states, so targeted validation is needed before escalating to broader controls.
evidence_summary: FL and WA IP Med/Surg rare cases totaled about $56K, mainly hernia K4090 at about $18K and trauma diagnoses S020XXA and S0211HB at about $24K combined.
FL and WA ACUTE HOSPITAL / TANF Standard added about $45K, with WA trauma cases adding about $17K and FL hernia or trauma cases adding about $28K.

business_patterns.what_is_impacting: NY / TANF Standard / ACUTE HOSPITAL / single provider concentration
key_driver_codes: Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy without C.D.E. without CC/MCC

impact_summary.volume_signal: 1 claim up from a very low base

business_patterns.pattern_details: In NY, one acute hospital provider accounts for nearly all of the identified increase in TANF Standard, and the same case appears in the clinical view. The episode is tied to laparoscopic cholecystectomy and diagnosis K8071 and shows a very high paid amount for a single claim. This is a provider-specific outlier until proven otherwise.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A single-provider spike is highly actionable because one case or payment issue can explain nearly all of the observed change.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review the full case and contract terms for PROVIDENCE CEDARS-SINAI TARZANA MEDICAL CENTER in NY TANF Standard and determine whether a provider-level payment correction or escalation is needed.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is concentrated in one provider and one claim, so it requires case-level confirmation before any broader provider action.
evidence_summary: NY TANF Standard acute hospital increase was about $51K, and about 98% of it was tied to PROVIDENCE CEDARS-SINAI TARZANA MEDICAL CENTER.
The same provider also drove a matching about $51K IP Med/Surg case tied to laparoscopic cholecystectomy and diagnosis K8071.
The signal is concentrated in 1 claim.

business_patterns.what_is_impacting: TN / LTSS Dual Eligible / SNF - FREE STANDING / single provider concentration
business_patterns.pattern_details: TN shows a concentrated SNF pattern at MCKENDREE SNF OPERATIONS LLC, with both higher operational spend and a matching NF rare-case signal. The claims are spread across multiple nervous system and post-acute diagnoses, which suggests provider-level placement or payment management rather than one unusual diagnosis alone. Because the signal sits on one provider, targeted provider action is more useful than marketwide policy.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Provider concentration creates a direct network and utilization lever without requiring statewide program changes.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Audit MCKENDREE SNF OPERATIONS LLC for placement, length of stay, and paid amount accuracy in LTSS Dual Eligible members, then decide whether provider outreach or contract remediation is warranted.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The provider signal is concentrated and the clinical and operational views may overlap, so targeted validation is required before expanding action.
evidence_summary: TN LTSS Dual Eligible / SNF - FREE STANDING added about $27K, with 17 more claims concentrated at MCKENDREE SNF OPERATIONS LLC.
TN NF rare cases added about $26K at the same provider across several nervous system and post-acute diagnoses.
Top TN NF diagnoses I69952 and S0630AS each added about $5K, confirming repeat provider concentration rather than a one-code anomaly.

business_patterns.top_pattern: FL and NY SNF low-volume spend emergence
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: NY ABD Non Dual and FL LTSS Dual Eligible / SNF - FREE STANDING
key_driver_codes: Other Digestive System Diagnoses without CC/MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Separate from the larger CA and TN patterns, NY and FL each show smaller SNF - FREE STANDING increases tied to digestive cases. Volumes are low, but both states show higher spend within specific Medicaid products, so these may be early site-of-care outliers. They are best handled as targeted SNF payment and utilization checks.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: These smaller SNF signals are manageable now and could become recurring cost drivers if payment or placement issues are left untreated.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run targeted postpay review on the NY and FL SNF episodes and compare paid amounts against applicable SNF payment rules for the identified products.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Both signals are low-baseline and small-volume, so they should be verified before being treated as durable trends.
evidence_summary: NY ABD Non Dual / SNF - FREE STANDING added about $25K on 3 claims, tied to Other Digestive System Diagnoses without CC/MCC.
FL LTSS Dual Eligible / SNF - FREE STANDING added about $23K on 6 claims, tied to the same digestive DRG.
Both state signals were flagged as low baseline and concentrated in a narrow SNF setting.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Not Mapped records are blocking clean action
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA and NJ / Not Mapped facility or clinical classification

impact_summary.volume_signal: claims up from a low base

business_patterns.pattern_details: Some of the remaining increase sits in records classified as Not Mapped for facility or clinical grouping. That limits confidence in site-of-care, provider, and clinical routing, especially in CA and NJ. Clean mapping is a gating step before tightening policy or escalating provider action on these claims.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If mapping is wrong, downstream UM, network, and clinical actions can be misdirected.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Correct facility and clinical mapping for the CA and NJ Not Mapped records, then reroute any confirmed claims to the appropriate UM, network, or clinical work queues.
business_patterns.validation_reason: These groups carry explicit unmapped or unknown flags, so data-quality correction is required before operational interpretation.
evidence_summary: CA LTSS Non Dual had about $9K of spend in Not Mapped facility records.
NJ TANF Standard had about $3K in Not Mapped facility records tied to RAJESH I PATEL.
NJ OP Surg also showed a separate Not Mapped clinical grouping tied to diagnosis D259 at about $3K.

executive_summary.headline: The main business story is concentrated acute and post-acute Medicaid spend growth in CA, plus smaller provider-specific and low-volume outliers in NY, TN, FL, and WA, with Not Mapped records creating a gating validation issue.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: Most of the identified increase is not broad-based utilization drift. It is concentrated in a few states, facility settings, providers, and rare clinical episodes, especially CA acute hospital and nursing-facility related cases. Business leaders should prioritize targeted inpatient, SNF, and provider payment reviews while fixing unmapped records before expanding policy changes.
recommended_focus_order: CA acute hospital inpatient pressure across TANF Standard and LTSS Non Dual
CA catastrophic IP Med/Surg and nursing-facility related rare cases
Provider-specific outliers in NY and TN, then clean up Not Mapped records in CA and NJ
